elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly states that Customer has “no minimum purchase ... commitment.”

elements.element: Customer has no minimum volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly disclaims any “volume commitment,” reinforced by Section 12.3’s acknowledgment that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.

elements.element: Customer is required to pay only for Services used or ordered.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 states that Customer “will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term.”

elements.element: If a minimum commitment applies, it is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: Section 2.1 eliminates all minimum purchase and volume commitments, so no commitment extends beyond—or applies during—the current term.

elements.element: If a minimum commitment applies, Customer may reduce it on 30 days’ notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Section 2.1 provides that Customer has no minimum commitment. Therefore, no commitment requires a reduction right.

elements.element: If a minimum commitment applies and Customer incurs a shortfall, the remedy is a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because there is no minimum commitment against which a shortfall, true-up, or penalty could arise.

result.reason: The operative redline replaces the three-year take-or-pay obligation with an express disclaimer of minimum purchase and volume commitments and limits payment to Services used or ordered. This fully reaches the preferred position; the commitment-specific fallback protections are also satisfied because their triggering condition is expressly absent. The change is confined to the offending commitment provision, leaves unrelated commercial terms intact, and is reinforced by Section 12.3. The non-operative margin comment does not affect the assessment.
